title.en: Tokens: how a model sees the world

subtitle.zh: 一句话进了模型，先被切碎再被计算。切法不是随机的——它由一套算法决定，并悄悄决定了你的成本、上限，和模型的大部分「怪癖」。
subtitle.en: A sentence is chopped into tokens before a model reads it — and the chopping is algorithmic, quietly deciding your cost, your limits, and most of the model's quirks.

h.zh: 从现象到机制：模型到底读到了什么

p.zh: 你输入「人工智能」，模型看到的不是 4 个汉字，也不是 1 个词，而是几个 token。Token 是训练前就用 BPE（Byte Pair Encoding，字节对编码）算法从海量文本里统计出来的高频碎片：算法从单个字符开始，反复把「最常一起出现的相邻片段」合并成新条目，直到词表被填满（通常 5 万～20 万条）。
p.en: Type 人工智能 and the model doesn't see 4 characters or 1 word but several tokens. Tokens are frequent fragments mined by BPE (Byte Pair Encoding) before training: starting from single bytes, the algorithm repeatedly merges the most frequent adjacent pair into a new entry until the vocabulary (usually 50k–200k entries) is full.

deep.zh: 为什么是这个算法？因为它是对「压缩」的贪心逼近：词表条目越能覆盖高频片段，同样一句话需要的 token 数越少，训练和推理的序列就越短、越便宜。所以词表不是语言学产物，是压缩经济学产物——英语语料占了大头，英语最「省钱」，中文里不常见的组合就碎。
deep.en: Why this algorithm? It is greedy compression: entries that cover frequent fragments shorten every sequence, making training and inference cheaper. A vocabulary is an artifact of compression economics, not linguistics — English dominates the corpus and stays cheap; rarer combinations fragment.

h.zh: 算一笔账：token 如何变成钱和时间
h.en: The math: how tokens become money and latency

p.zh: 三件事都按 token 记账。计价：主流模型按「每百万 token」报价，输入通常比输出便宜 3～5 倍。上限：上下文窗口（模型一次能处理的总量）也按 token 计，你的提问、贴进来的文档、历史对话、回复，全部挤占同一个窗口。速度：生成是逐 token 进行的，回复快慢直接正比于输出 token 数。
p.en: Three things are billed in tokens. Pricing: mainstream models quote per million tokens, with input usually 3–5x cheaper than output. Limits: the context window — everything you type, paste, and the whole conversation plus the reply — shares one token budget. Latency: generation proceeds token by token, so speed tracks output length.

h.zh: 实例

p.zh: 把一份 8000 字的合同贴给模型问问题：中文按 1 字 ≈ 1～1.5 token 算，这份合同 ≈ 1 万 token，还没提问就吃掉约 1 万 token 输入。若输入价 $1/百万 token，单次成本约 $0.01——便宜，但如果这段对话要重复 20 轮，且每轮都重复贴合同，成本和窗口占用就放大 20 倍。省法子：把合同摘要成 500 字再贴，token 降为约 1/20。
p.en: Paste an 8,000-character contract into a chat: at roughly 1–1.5 tokens per Chinese character it is ≈10k tokens of input before you even ask. At $1/M input tokens that is about $0.01 per call — trivial, until the same contract rides along for 20 turns, multiplying cost and window usage 20x. Fix: summarize to 500 characters first; tokens drop to 1/20.

h.zh: 怪癖的根源：模型看到的不是你以为的
h.en: Why quirks happen: the model sees something else

p.zh: 让模型数「strawberry 里有几个 r」，它常答错——不是它笨，是它看到的根本不是 s-t-r-a-w-b-e-r-r-y 这个字母序列，而是类似「str」「aw」「berry」的 token 序列。每个 token 对它是一个不可再分的编号，字母信息只在编号背后隐约存在，所以它必须「猜」每个块里有几个字母。
p.en: Ask a model how many r's are in strawberry and it may fail — not because it is dumb, but because it never sees s-t-r-a-w-b-e-r-r-y. It sees tokens like str / aw / berry, atomic IDs whose letters are only faintly implied, so it must guess what hides inside each chunk.

h.zh: 常见误区

p.zh: 「模型认识单词」。对模型来说没有单词，只有 token 编号序列。同理，「模型知道自己的字数上限」也不成立——它感知不到 token 边界，超限会被硬截断，而不是礼貌地告诉你。写长文时主动分段、主动要求「先列大纲再逐段写」，本质都是在帮它管理 token。
p.en: “The model knows words.” It doesn't — only token-ID sequences. Likewise it cannot feel its own length limit: overflow is hard truncation, not a polite warning. Asking for an outline first, then section by section, is really token management on its behalf.

h.zh: 延伸：这个知识点连向哪里

p.zh: Token 是后面几乎所有主题的地基：第 3 天的「温度与采样」发生在每个 token 的选择上；第 4 天的「上下文窗口」是 token 预算的分配问题；阶段二的「上下文工程」本质是 token 的经济学；阶段三 Agent 的工具调用输出也是一串 token。今天只需带走一句话——
p.en: Tokens underpin everything ahead: sampling (day 3) happens per token; the context window (day 4) is a token budget; context engineering (stage 2) is token economics; agent tool calls (stage 3) are also token streams. For today, one sentence is enough —

h.zh: 动手（15 分钟）

p.zh: 打开 tokenizer 演示页（搜 “OpenAI tokenizer”），依次输入三组内容并记录 token 数：① 「人工智能」vs「artificial intelligence」；② 你的名字；③ 一段 100 字的自我介绍。然后用一句话回答：为什么第 ③ 组的平均「每词 token 数」比第 ① 组高？（提示：词表里谁的语料多）
p.en: Open a tokenizer demo (search “OpenAI tokenizer”) and record token counts for: (1) 人工智能 vs artificial intelligence; (2) your name; (3) a 100-character self-intro. Then answer in one sentence: why is the tokens-per-word ratio higher in (3) than (1)? (Hint: whose corpus filled the vocabulary?)

takeaway.zh: Token 是模型的记账单位，也是压缩的产物：成本、窗口、速度、怪癖，全都从「切法」来。
takeaway.en: Tokens are the model's unit of account — and an artifact of compression: cost, windows, speed and quirks all follow from the cut.

sentence.zh: 先把事看清，再把话说清。
sentence.en: Understand it first. Then explain it plainly.

coverHook.zh: 同样的 12 个字，中文 10 个 token，英文 11 个——账单不一样。
coverHook.en: Same 12 characters: 10 tokens in Chinese, 11 in English — and different bills.

title.en: Embeddings: words move into a coordinate system

subtitle.zh: Token 编号只是门牌号。真正让模型「懂意思」的，是门牌后面那张坐标表：每个 token 对应一串数字，意思相近的词在空间里挨得近——语义从此可以做几何运算。
subtitle.en: A token ID is just a house number. What lets a model "understand" is the table behind it: every token maps to a vector, similar meanings sit close together, and meaning becomes geometry you can compute on.

h.zh: 机制：每个 token 领到一串坐标
h.en: Mechanism: every token gets a vector

p.zh: 模型里有一张「嵌入表」（embedding table）：行数等于词表大小（比如 20 万行），每行是一个稠密向量（常见 768～4096 维，如 GPT 系小模型 768 维、嵌入服务常见 1536 维）。Token 进模型的第一步就是拿自己的编号去查表，把 ID 换成一个向量。「意思相近」用余弦相似度衡量：两个向量夹角越小（方向越一致），分数越接近 1。这张表不是人编的——训练开始时全是随机数，随着模型不断预测下一个词，相关词的向量被反复一起挪动，几千维的空间自己长出结构。
p.en: Inside the model sits an embedding table: one row per vocabulary entry (say 200k rows), each row a dense vector (commonly 768–4096 dimensions; embedding APIs often use 1536). A token's first step in the model is to look up its ID and become that vector. "Similar meaning" is measured by cosine similarity: the smaller the angle between two vectors, the closer the score is to 1. Nobody writes this table — it starts random, and as the model practices predicting the next word, related tokens get nudged together until geometry emerges.

deep.zh: 为什么必须用向量，不能直接用编号？因为神经网络只会算数。编号 200 和 201 在数学上毫无关系，20 万维的 one-hot 编码也互相等距——「猫」和「狗」的距离和「猫」和「量子」一样远，语义信息量是零。稠密向量把 20 万个互相孤立的门牌压进两千维、远近有序的空间，这又是压缩经济学：几何结构就是学到的统计规律。「国王 − 男人 + 女人 ≈ 女王」这类经典结果说明，语义关系真的以「方向」的形式存在于这个空间里。
deep.en: Why vectors instead of raw IDs? Because networks only compute numbers. IDs 200 and 201 share nothing mathematically, and one-hot encodings are all equidistant — "cat" is as far from "dog" as from "quantum". Dense vectors compress 200k isolated labels into a ~2k-dimensional space with structure, again compression economics: the geometry IS the learned statistics. Classic results like king − man + woman ≈ queen show semantic relations really exist as directions in this space.

h.zh: 实例：把整个知识库变成坐标，不到一杯咖啡钱
h.en: Worked example: embedding a whole knowledge base for pocket change

p.zh: 假设你有 1 万条 FAQ，每条平均 60 token，想把它们变成可检索的知识库：用嵌入 API 全部向量化，共 60 万 token。按主流嵌入模型约 $0.02/百万 token 计价，成本约 $0.012——一次付清，之后不用再算。之后每次用户提问，只把问题本身（约 20 token）向量化，再在 1 万个向量里找余弦最近的几条。检索不是逐条「读」，而是先算 1 万次点积再排序——向量化之后，找相似从「阅读理解」变成了「量距离」。
p.en: Say you have 10,000 FAQ entries averaging 60 tokens and want them searchable: embed them all via an embedding API — 600k tokens total. At roughly $0.02 per million tokens that is about $0.012, paid once. Each user question afterwards embeds just itself (~20 tokens), then you find the few nearest entries by cosine similarity. Retrieval is no longer "reading" 10k entries — it is computing 10k dot products and sorting: similarity search turns comprehension into measuring distance.

h.zh: 实例

p.zh: 同样的 1 万条 FAQ，如果不用向量：让模型每次把全部条目读一遍再回答，60 万 token × 每次提问都付一遍，问 100 次就是 6000 万 token 的输入费；向量化方案同样的 100 次提问只多花 100 × 20 = 2000 token 的嵌入费。差距约 3 万倍——这就是「先向量化、再检索」存在的理由。
p.en: Without vectors, a model would reread all 600k tokens on every question; 100 questions cost 60M input tokens. The vector route embeds 100 × 20 = 2k tokens for the same 100 questions — a gap of roughly 30,000x. That is why "embed first, retrieve second" exists.

h.zh: 误区：距离近 ≠ 意思相同
h.en: Misconception: close in space ≠ same in meaning

p.zh: 余弦相似度是统计关系，不是同义词判断。「好评」和「差评」语义相反，却常常出现在几乎相同的语境里（都跟「商品」「体验」「推荐」搭配），所以向量可能挨得很近——嵌入模型分不清褒贬，只认语境分布。反过来，同一个词在不同语境里其实「该」有不同坐标，早期静态嵌入给一个词只留一行，一词多义就被压扁了（后来的动态/上下文化嵌入为此而生）。
p.en: Cosine similarity captures statistical co-occurrence, not synonymy. "Great review" and "terrible review" are opposites yet live in nearly identical contexts (products, experiences, recommendations), so their embeddings can sit close — the model knows distribution, not sentiment. And one word in different contexts deserves different coordinates; static embeddings give each word one row, flattening polysemy (contextualized embeddings exist to fix this).

h.zh: 常见误区

p.zh: 「向量维度越高越好」。维度高只是容量大：300 维的词向量早已能表达大部分语义关系，1536 维相对 768 维的提升是边际的，代价却是存储和检索成本翻倍。选嵌入模型看的是检索质量基准和你的预算，不是维度数字。另外，嵌入只是「把意思变成坐标」，它不记忆任何事实——知识库本身还是存在你那边的普通文本里。
p.en: "More dimensions are always better." Dimension is capacity, not quality: 300-dim vectors already capture most semantic relations; 1536 vs 768 is marginal while storage and search costs double. Pick embedding models by retrieval benchmarks and budget, not dimension counts. And remember: an embedding stores coordinates, not facts — your knowledge base still lives as plain text on your side.

h.zh: 延伸：向量是后面 166 天的底座

p.zh: Embedding 是后面几乎所有主题的承重墙：第 3 天的「温度与采样」发生在向量穿过几十层网络之后的输出分布上；阶段四 RAG 的核心动作「检索」就是余弦相似度排序，今天算过的账就是它的成本模型；阶段三 Agent 的长期记忆，本质是把历史对话存成向量、用得着的时候再按距离取回。今天带走一句话——
p.en: Embeddings carry almost everything ahead: sampling (day 3) happens on the output distribution after vectors pass through dozens of layers; RAG (stage 4) is cosine-similarity ranking, and today's math is its cost model; agent long-term memory (stage 3) stores past dialogue as vectors and recalls by distance. One sentence for today —

h.zh: 动手（15 分钟）

p.zh: 找一个嵌入演示（搜 “OpenAI embeddings” 或 TensorFlow Embedding Projector），把三组词向量化并记录余弦相似度：① 「猫」和「狗」；② 「猫」和「汽车」；③ 「国王」「男人」「女人」「女王」，算一算 国王−男人+女人 是否最接近女王。然后回答：为什么 ① 的分数高不奇怪，而 ③ 能成立才真正说明向量学到了「关系」？（提示：②是「词与词」的距离，③是「方向与方向」的对齐——差向量画在纸上，看它们是否平行。）
p.en: Open an embedding demo (search "OpenAI embeddings" or TensorFlow Embedding Projector) and record cosine similarities for: (1) cat/dog; (2) cat/car; (3) king, man, woman, queen — check whether king − man + woman lands nearest queen. Then answer: why is (1) unsurprising, while (3) working is the real evidence vectors learned relations? (Hint: (2) is word-to-word distance, (3) is direction-to-direction alignment — sketch the difference vectors and check whether they run parallel.)

takeaway.zh: 向量把「意思」变成几何：模型不认识词，它只是把语料里的统计关系摆进了一个几千维的空间。
takeaway.en: Embeddings turn meaning into geometry: the model doesn't know words — it arranges corpus statistics inside a few-thousand-dimensional space.

title.zh: 温度与采样：模型怎么决定下一个词
title.en: Temperature & sampling: how the next word gets picked

subtitle.zh: 模型每写一个字都要掷一次骰子，而骰子不是均匀的——logits 加温度决定每一面的概率。这根旋钮不花一分钱，却同时管着稳定的下限和胡说的上限。
subtitle.en: Every token is one roll of a loaded die: logits plus temperature set each face's odds. The dial costs nothing, yet it governs both the floor of reliability and the ceiling of nonsense.

h.zh: 机制：softmax 与温度

p.zh: 模型写每个字之前，先给词表里 20 万个候选各打一个分（logit，可正可负），再跑一遍 softmax：把每个分数变成 e 的幂（全变正数、不改变大小顺序），除以总和归一化成概率，最后按概率掷骰子选出一个。温度只做一件事——取指数之前把所有 logit 除以 T。T<1 把分差放大，概率向头部集中；T>1 把分差压平，尾部词被抬高。关键在概率比：两个候选的概率比是 e^((a−b)/T)，0.6 的分差在 T=1 时对应 1.8 倍，在 T=2 时只剩 1.35 倍——温度就是「分差换概率」的汇率。
p.en: Before writing each token, the model scores all ~200k vocabulary candidates with a logit (positive or negative), then runs softmax: exponentiate each score (all positive, order preserved), normalize into probabilities, and sample one. Temperature does exactly one thing — divide every logit by T before the exponent. T<1 widens the gaps and piles probability onto the head; T>1 flattens them and lifts the tail. The key is the probability ratio: e^((a−b)/T). A 0.6-logit gap means 1.8x odds at T=1 but only 1.35x at T=2 — temperature is the exchange rate between score gaps and probability.

deep.zh: 为什么用 e 的幂而不直接归一化？logit 有正有负，直接归一化会出负概率；exp 既保正又保序，还让「分差」以乘法方式进入概率比，数学上最干净。而温度放进分母而不是另设一套参数，意味着它不需要重新训练——同一组 logit，拧一下 T 就得到从保守到放飞的一整族分布。这正是它被做成「旋钮」而不是「开关」的原因：连续可调，且与训练解耦。
deep.en: Why exponentiate instead of normalizing directly? Logits go negative; a plain normalization would produce negative probabilities. exp is positive, order-preserving, and lets score gaps enter the probability ratio multiplicatively — mathematically the cleanest choice. And because temperature sits in the denominator rather than being a trained parameter, it needs no retraining: one set of logits, one turn of T, a whole family of distributions from cautious to wild. That is why it ships as a dial, not a switch.

h.zh: 实例：三种温度三张账单
h.en: Worked example: three temperatures, three bills

p.zh: 让模型补「今天天气真＿」，设候选 logit 为：热 5.2、不错 4.6、好 4.4、差 3.8、蓝 3.0（ softmax 实算）。T=0.5：「热」63.4%，生成 100 次约 63 次是它，「蓝」只有 0.8%；T=1：「热」42.5%，「蓝」升到 4.7%；T=2：「热」只剩 30.9%，「蓝」翻到 10.3%——每 10 次就有 1 次说出「天气真蓝」。注意成本一分未变：温度改变的是「选哪个 token」，不是「选多少 token」，账单只看 token 数。
p.en: Complete “今天天气真＿” with logits 热 5.2, 不错 4.6, 好 4.4, 差 3.8, 蓝 3.0 (real softmax). T=0.5: “热” takes 63.4% — about 63 of 100 runs — and “蓝” just 0.8%. T=1: “热” 42.5%, “蓝” 4.7%. T=2: “热” down to 30.9% while “蓝” climbs to 10.3% — “really blue” appears once every 10 draws. The bill never changes: temperature alters which token gets picked, not how many — you pay per token either way.

h.zh: 实例

p.zh: 翻译成产品决策：代码补全要可预测，团队普遍压到 T=0～0.3，同样的输入给出稳定输出、可写进测试；客服问答取 T≈0.7，稳中带一点自然；头脑风暴开到 T≥1.0。同一个模型，价格相同，性格由这根旋钮决定——所以「换个模型试试」之前，先拧温度，它是免费的。
p.en: As a product decision: code completion wants predictability, so teams run T=0–0.3 — same input, stable output, testable; customer-facing chat sits near T=0.7; brainstorming opens at T≥1.0. Same model, same price, different personality — so before “try another model”, turn the dial; it's free.

h.zh: 误区：高温不等于高创造力

p.zh: 最常见的误读是「温度越高越有创造力」。温度不提供任何新知识，它只决定采样时往概率分布的尾部走多远，而尾部堆的大多不是妙语，是语法垃圾和事实错误。创造力的上限来自模型学到的分布本身：分布里没有的联想，拧到 T=3 也拧不出来；分布里有的好东西，低温度照样能选中。越过临界点后，多出来的不是创意，是幻觉率。
p.en: The most common misreading: “higher temperature = more creativity.” Temperature adds no knowledge; it only sets how far into the distribution's tail you sample — and the tail holds mostly grammatical debris and factual errors, not brilliance. The ceiling of creativity comes from the distribution the model learned: an association absent from it won't appear at T=3, and good ones get picked at low T anyway. Past the tipping point, what rises isn't creativity — it's the hallucination rate.

h.zh: 常见误区

p.zh: 「模型想好了再写」。其实没有想好这回事——每个 token 都是一次独立掷骰，包括它「计划」要写的那些字本身，所谓规划也只是被采样出来的 token。同理，「温度 0 就绝对确定」也不严谨：贪心采样消除了采样随机性，但 GPU 并行计算的浮点误差仍可能让两次运行结果不同。
p.en: “The model plans, then writes.” There is no planning step — every token is an independent roll of the die, including the tokens that look like a plan. And “temperature 0 is fully deterministic” is also too strong: greedy sampling removes sampling randomness, but floating-point nondeterminism in GPU parallel math can still make two runs differ.

h.zh: 延伸：旋钮后面还有一排开关

p.zh: 温度是采样家族里最基础的一个。下一步是 top-p / top-k：先按概率截断候选池、把尾部物理切除，再在剩下的池子里采样，与温度配合使用——温度调「形状」，截断管「下限」。往后看：阶段二的提示工程会把温度当作提示词之外的第一根控制杆；阶段三 Agent 调用工具几乎总用低温，工具参数写错了没有「创意」可言；阶段四 RAG 的回答要贴着检索到的事实，同样压低温度。今天带走一句话——
p.en: Temperature is the most basic member of the sampling family. Next come top-p / top-k: cut the candidate pool by probability first — physically removing the tail — then sample what's left, combined with temperature: the dial shapes the distribution, the cut guards the floor. Ahead: stage 2 treats temperature as the first control beyond the prompt; stage 3 agents call tools almost always at low temperature — wrong tool arguments have no “creativity” to offer; stage 4 RAG answers must stick to retrieved facts, so temperature stays low. One sentence for today —

h.zh: 动手（15 分钟）

p.zh: 打开任意带温度参数的 playground 或 API 调试台，用提示「今天天气真＿」在 T=0.2、T=1.0、T=1.8 各生成 10 次，记录每次补出的词。回答：为什么 T=0.2 的 10 次几乎全同，而 T=1.8 出现了「蓝」？（提示：0.6 的 logit 分差在 T=0.2 时对应 e³≈20 倍的概率比，在 T=1.8 时只剩 1.4 倍——尾部的词被放大了多少？）
p.en: Open any playground with a temperature slider and complete “今天天气真＿” 10 times each at T=0.2, T=1.0 and T=1.8, recording every completion. Then answer: why are the T=0.2 runs nearly identical while T=1.8 produces “蓝”? (Hint: a 0.6-logit gap maps to a ~20x probability ratio at T=0.2 but only ~1.4x at T=1.8 — how much did the tail get amplified?)

takeaway.zh: 模型每写一个字都掷一次骰子，温度决定骰子的形状：它放大或抹平分差，给不了新知识，只决定你离分布的头部多远。
takeaway.en: Every token is a roll of a weighted die, and temperature shapes the die: it widens or flattens the gaps, adds no knowledge — it only sets how far from the top of the distribution you land.

hook.zh: 同一个模型，拧一下温度，就换了性格。
hook.en: Same model, one turn of the temperature dial — a new personality.

temperatures.noteZh: T=0.5：分差被放大，概率向头部集中——保守、可复现。
temperatures.noteEn: T=0.5: gaps amplified, probability piles onto the head — conservative, reproducible.

temperatures.noteZh: T=1：softmax 的原始输出，模型出厂时的默认性格。
temperatures.noteEn: T=1: the raw softmax output — the model's factory-default personality.

temperatures.noteZh: T=2：尾部被抬高，「天气真蓝」每 10 次出现 1 次。
temperatures.noteEn: T=2: the tail is lifted — “really blue” shows up once every 10 draws.

note.zh: 概率由真实 softmax 计算得出：logit 除以温度后归一化。
note.en: Probabilities computed by a real softmax: divide logits by temperature, then normalize.

coverHook.zh: 同一句话，T=0.5 时「热」占 63%，T=2 时只剩 31%。
coverHook.en: Same sentence: “hot” takes 63% at T=0.5, only 31% at T=2.

title.zh: 上下文窗口：128K 到底装得下什么
title.en: The context window: what 128K actually holds

subtitle.zh: 上下文窗口是一个按 token 记账的硬预算：你的提问、贴进来的文档、全部历史对话和模型的回复，挤占同一笔额度。写满了不会得到提醒，只会被从头上悄悄截断。
subtitle.en: The context window is a hard budget measured in tokens: your question, the pasted documents, the whole conversation history and the reply all draw from one pool. When it runs out you get no warning — the head is silently truncated.

h.zh: 机制：同一笔预算里的四笔开销
h.en: Mechanism: four expenses out of one budget

p.zh: 所谓「上下文」，是模型一次能读到的全部文本：系统提示、你的提问、贴进去的文档、之前每一轮对话、以及它自己要生成的回复——四样东西拼接成一个 token 序列，共享同一个窗口上限。窗口不是记忆，是工作台：这一轮结束后，桌面上的一切都会被撤走，下一轮原样重新摆一遍，这就是为什么长对话越到后面越慢（每轮都要重读全部历史）、也越贵（按全部历史付输入费）。窗口大小从 8K 到 128K，再到 1M token 不等——但无论多大，游戏规则相同。
p.en: "Context" is everything the model reads in one shot: system prompt, your question, pasted documents, every earlier turn, and the reply it must generate — spliced into one token sequence sharing a single ceiling. The window is not memory; it is a workbench. After each turn the bench is cleared and rebuilt from scratch next turn — which is why long chats get slower (the whole history is reread every turn) and pricier (input is billed on the entire history). Windows run from 8K to 128K to 1M tokens — but the rules of the game never change.

deep.zh: 为什么满了是从头上截断？模型没有「文件系统」可以回翻——它一次只能看到当前送进来的序列，序列超长，最省事也最常用的做法就是把最旧的部分切掉。这带来一个反直觉的后果：对话开头的约定、贴过的关键文档，恰恰是最先消失的部分。模型不是「忘了」，是压根没被喂到——它对被截断这件事零感知，不会告诉你「我没看到那个文件」，只会基于剩下的内容一本正经地继续。
deep.en: Why does the head get cut? The model has no filesystem to page back through — it only sees the sequence it is fed this turn, and when that sequence overflows, dropping the oldest chunk is the cheapest, most common fix. The counterintuitive result: the opening agreements and key documents from early in a chat are the first to vanish. The model didn't "forget" — it was never fed them. It has zero awareness of the truncation, never says "I can't see that file", and simply carries on, confidently, on what remains.

h.zh: 实例：一份 400 页 PDF 塞不塞得进 128K？
h.en: Worked example: does a 400-page PDF fit in 128K?

p.zh: 128K 窗口 ≈ 131,072 token。英文按 1 token ≈ 0.75 词算，约 9.8 万词；400 页学术 PDF 平均每页 600 词，共 24 万词——超窗口 2.4 倍，整本塞不进去。中文更吃亏：1 汉字 ≈ 1～1.5 token，128K 只装 8 万～12 万字，相当于 160～240 页。这笔账的结论不是「窗口没用」，而是「窗口是配给制」：整本塞不进，就先分段——每段让模型做 500 字摘要，40 段摘要共 2 万 token，轻松进窗口，再让模型基于摘要回答。两遍读法（map-reduce）用 1/12 的 token 覆盖了同样的内容。
p.en: A 128K window is ≈131,072 tokens. At 1 token ≈ 0.75 English words that is about 98k words; a 400-page academic PDF averages 600 words per page — 240k words total, 2.4x over the ceiling. Chinese fares worse: 1 character ≈ 1–1.5 tokens, so 128K holds only 80k–120k characters, roughly 160–240 pages. The lesson isn't "windows are useless" but "windows are rationing": since the whole book won't fit, chunk it first — have the model summarize each chunk to 500 characters, 40 summaries ≈ 20k tokens, easily inside the window, then answer from the summaries. The two-pass (map-reduce) read covers the same content on 1/12 the tokens.

h.zh: 实例

p.zh: 把窗口当钱包算一笔对话账：系统提示 500 token + 每轮你的问题 100 token + 回复 400 token。第 1 轮付输入 600，第 2 轮付 1,100（上一轮也在场）……第 50 轮输入涨到 25,100，50 轮累计输入费 63.9 万 token——占掉半个 128K 窗口。省法子是定期开新对话并把结论粘过去：20 轮一切换，同样的 50 轮只要 4.7 万 token，省 26%。
p.en: Treat the window like a wallet: system prompt 500 tokens + 100 per question + 400 per reply. Turn 1 bills 600 input tokens, turn 2 bills 1,100 (the previous turn is still on the bench)… turn 50 bills 25,100; 50 turns total ≈ 639k input tokens — half a 128K window. The fix: start a fresh chat every ~20 turns carrying conclusions over; the same 50 turns cost ≈ 47k tokens, a 26% saving.

h.zh: 误区：窗口大 ≠ 记性好
h.en: Misconception: a big window ≠ a good memory

p.zh: 厂商把窗口从 8K 卷到 1M，很多人随之相信「能装下就能用好」。真实情况有两条裂缝：其一，有效窗口往往小于标称窗口——「大海捞针」类测试显示，就算关键信息明明躺在窗口深处，模型对中段内容的召回率也明显低于首尾（位置偏差，中间内容被注意力稀释）；其二，装满的窗口又慢又贵：128K 全满的一次调用，输入费是 4K 调用的 32 倍，首 token 延迟也明显拉长。窗口是货架面积，不是记忆能力——货架再大，管理库存的仍然是你。
p.en: As vendors raced from 8K to 1M, many concluded "if it fits, it works." Two cracks in that belief: first, the effective window is often smaller than the advertised one — needle-in-a-haystack tests show recall clearly drops for content buried in the middle even when it sits well inside the window (positional bias: middle content gets diluted by attention); second, a full window is slow and expensive — one 128K-full call bills 32x the input of a 4K call, with visibly longer time-to-first-token. The window is shelf space, not memory — however big the shelf, you are still the inventory manager.

h.zh: 常见误区

p.zh: 「窗口越大，模型就越聪明」。窗口只决定「一次能看多少」，不改变「看懂多少」：把 1M token 一次倒进去，推理能力没有增加，反而因为关键信息稀释在噪声里更容易答错。同理，「新对话开在同一个会话里就继承了记忆」也不成立——每个会话的窗口从零开始装，跨会话的记忆要靠你显式粘贴或外部存储（这连向阶段三 Agent 的记忆系统）。
p.en: "A bigger window makes the model smarter." The window sets how much it sees at once, not how well it reasons: dumping 1M tokens in at once adds no reasoning power and makes errors more likely as the signal drowns in noise. And "a new chat in the same session inherits memory" is also false — every conversation fills its window from zero; cross-session memory needs explicit pasting or external storage (leading to stage 3's agent memory).

h.zh: 延伸：窗口经济学贯穿后面 164 天

p.zh: 上下文窗口是后面所有主题的成本模型：阶段二的「上下文工程」就是把有限窗口留给最高价值 token 的排兵布阵；阶段三 Agent 要处理「工具输出爆炸」——一次网页抓取 1 万 token，几轮就把窗口吃穿，需要摘要与丢弃策略；阶段四 RAG 存在的合法性直接来自今天：既然窗口装不下整个知识库，就把「最相关的几段」在每次提问时现场搬进窗口——检索本质上是为窗口选料。今天带走一句话——
p.en: The context window is the cost model for everything ahead: stage 2's context engineering is the art of allocating the finite window to the highest-value tokens; stage 3 agents face tool-output explosions — one web scrape is 10k tokens, a few turns gut the window, so summaries and eviction policies are needed; stage 4 RAG exists precisely because of today: since no window holds a whole knowledge base, retrieval fetches the most relevant few passages into the window on demand — retrieval is ingredient selection for the window. One sentence for today —

h.zh: 动手（15 分钟）

p.zh: 找一个显示 token 计数的聊天界面（多数 playground 有），连续就同一主题追问 10 轮，记录每轮显示的上下文 token 数。回答：为什么第 10 轮的计数远大于你 10 个问题的字数总和？（提示：窗口里还坐着谁——系统提示、每一轮的回复、可能贴过的材料，全都在按 token 计房租。）
p.en: Open a chat UI that shows token counts (most playgrounds do) and ask follow-ups on one topic for 10 straight turns, recording the context token count each turn. Then answer: why is turn 10's count far larger than the sum of your 10 questions' characters? (Hint: who else sits in the window — the system prompt, every reply so far, any pasted material — all paying rent in tokens.)

takeaway.zh: 上下文窗口是按 token 记账的硬预算，不是记忆：写满从头上截断，装满又贵又钝——管理这笔预算的人是你。
takeaway.en: The context window is a hard token budget, not memory: overflow silently truncates from the head, and a full window is slow and expensive — you are the budget's manager.

hook.zh: 窗口写满时，没有人会提醒你。
hook.en: When the window fills, nobody warns you.

sentence.zh: 同一笔 token 预算，四笔开销。

note.zh: 示意：窗口 16 格。历史逐轮增长，第 3 轮起超出预算——最旧的历史格先被截断，且不会提醒你。
note.en: Illustrative: a 16-cell window. History grows every turn; from turn 3 it overflows — the oldest cells are truncated first, with no warning.

coverHook.zh: 400 页 PDF 塞不进 128K 窗口：超了 2.4 倍，写满也不会有提醒。
coverHook.en: A 400-page PDF doesn't fit in 128K: 2.4x over — and no warning when it fills.

title.zh: 梯度下降：模型是怎么学会的
title.en: Gradient descent: how a model actually learns

subtitle.zh: 模型不是背会的，是改错的：预测 → 量化误差（损失）→ 沿坡最陡方向微调参数 → 亿万次重复。看懂这条下坡曲线，就看懂了所有训练的骨架。
subtitle.en: A model doesn't memorize — it corrects: predict, measure the error (loss), nudge every parameter down the steepest slope, repeat billions of times. Read this downhill curve and you've read the skeleton of all training.

h.zh: 机制：误差在哪里，坡就朝哪里

p.zh: 训练循环只有三步。① 预测：参数当前的值给出一个答案；② 损失：拿答案和标准答案算一个误差分数（loss），比如交叉熵——第 3 天算过的 softmax 概率，正是交叉熵的输入；③ 更新：对每个参数求「损失对它的导数」（梯度），它告诉你这个参数往哪个方向动一点、误差会变大还是变小。梯度下降就做一件事：每个参数往梯度的反方向挪一小步。挪动量 = 学习率 × 梯度，步长由学习率决定——它是训练里最重要的那根旋钮。
p.en: The training loop is three steps. 1) Predict: current parameters produce an answer. 2) Loss: score the answer against ground truth (for example cross-entropy — the softmax probabilities you computed on day 3 are exactly its input). 3) Update: take the derivative of loss with respect to each parameter (the gradient), which tells you which direction a nudge makes the error worse. Gradient descent does one thing: move every parameter a small step in the opposite direction. Step size = learning rate × gradient — the learning rate is the single most important dial in training.

deep.zh: 为什么是「反方向的一小步」，而不是直接解出最优参数？因为参数量太大——现代模型几十亿个参数联立，方程解不出来；但「每个参数在当前位置的坡度」算得出（微积分链式法则，工程名叫反向传播）。所以训练从求解问题退化为导航问题：不知道谷底在哪，但每一步都能摸清脚下朝哪最陡，就顺着下坡走。这条曲线刻画的就是「误差随训练步数下降」——前几百步陡降，之后越来越平：容易的规律先学会（语法、高频搭配），剩下的误差越来越难榨。
deep.en: Why a small step opposite the gradient instead of solving for the optimum directly? Scale: modern models couple billions of parameters — no closed-form solution exists. But the slope at the current position is computable (calculus chain rule, known in engineering as backpropagation). Training thus degrades from solving to navigating: you never know where the valley floor is, but you can always feel the steepest direction underfoot. The curve plots loss over training steps: a steep early drop, then flattening — easy regularities (grammar, frequent pairings) get learned first; what remains is progressively harder to squeeze out.

h.zh: 算一笔账：一次「学习」要付多少算力
h.en: Worked example: the compute bill of one training run

p.zh: 把数字摆出来才知道训练有多贵。一次训练要把整个语料过很多遍（每遍叫一个 epoch）。假设一个 7B 参数的小模型、1 万亿 token 语料：业界经验公式（Chinchilla）建议至少约 20 倍参数量的 token，即 1400 亿 token 起步；按训练每参数每 token 约 6 次浮点运算估算，共 7×10⁹ × 1.4×10¹¹ × 6 ≈ 5.9×10²⁰ 次运算。一张 RTX 4090 每秒约 8×10¹⁴ 次有效运算，单卡要跑 20 多年——所以真实训练是几千张卡并行几周到几个月。这就是大模型经济学的前提：预训练贵到只有少数人做得起，推理便宜到人人可分摊。
p.en: Put numbers on it. One pass over the corpus is an epoch; a real run does many. Take a 7B-parameter model on a 1-trillion-token corpus: the Chinchilla rule of thumb suggests at least ~20 tokens per parameter — 140B tokens; at ~6 FLOPs per parameter per token that is 7×10⁹ × 1.4×10¹¹ × 6 ≈ 5.9×10²⁰ operations. An RTX 4090 delivers ~8×10¹⁴ effective FLOP/s — a single card would need 20+ years. Real training runs thousands of GPUs in parallel for weeks to months. That is the premise of LLM economics: pretraining is so expensive only a few can do it, while inference is cheap enough for everyone to share.

h.zh: 实例

p.zh: 学习率怎么毁掉一次训练，用一条一维曲线就能看清：设损失 f(w)=(w−3)²，最优解 w=3。学习率 0.8：从 w=0 出发，第一步跳到 4.8（过头），第二步跳回 1.44……来回震荡、幅度越来越小，最终收敛；学习率 2.0：第一步跳到 9（过头一倍），第二步跳到 −3，越跳越远——发散，损失不降反升。同一模型、同一数据，唯一差别是一根旋钮。
p.en: Watch the learning rate destroy a run on a one-dimensional curve: f(w)=(w−3)², optimum at w=3. With lr=0.8 starting at w=0: step to 4.8 (overshoot), back to 1.44… oscillating with shrinking amplitude, converging. With lr=2.0: step to 9 (double overshoot), then −3 — diverging, loss rising. Same model, same data, one dial.

h.zh: 误区：模型不是「越来越聪明」，是在「降损失」
h.en: Misconception: the model isn't getting smarter — it's lowering a number

p.zh: 最流行的误解是把训练想象成「喂养知识」：喂语料、模型变聪明。真实发生的只是：调整几千亿个旋钮，让「预测下一个 token」这个单一目标的分数下降。所有你以为的「智能」，都是这个单一优化目标的副产品。这解释了两件事：其一，为什么模型会一本正经地编造事实（幻觉）——「说个听起来对的下一句」在统计上得分很高，损失函数从不检查真假；其二，为什么模型的知识冻结在训练截止日——之后的世界它没见过，没有梯度，就没有学习。
p.en: The most popular misreading is training as feeding knowledge: pour in the corpus, the model gets smart. What actually happens: thousands of knobs are tuned to lower one score — the loss of predicting the next token. Everything you recognize as intelligence is a byproduct of that single objective. This explains two things: why models invent facts with total confidence (hallucination) — a plausible-sounding next token scores well statistically, and the loss never checks truth; and why knowledge freezes at the training cutoff — the world after it produced no gradients, hence no learning.

h.zh: 常见误区

p.zh: 「损失越低，模型越好用」。不一定。损失降到 3.2 后继续磨到 3.1，多半只是把语料背得更熟，通用能力未必提升，过拟合风险反而涨——训练曲线漂亮不等于下游好用，业界判断模型好不好要另跑基准测试。同理，「训练完了模型就定型」也不准确：预训练之后的对齐微调（SFT/RLHF）是另一段训练，它用人类反馈构造新的损失函数，把「会接话」的模型掰成「愿意配合、说人话」的助手——那是第 8 天的主题。
p.en: Lower loss means a better model — not necessarily. Grinding from 3.2 to 3.1 often just memorizes the corpus harder: general capability may not move while overfitting risk rises. A pretty training curve is not downstream quality, which is why benchmarks exist. And the model is fixed after training — also wrong: alignment fine-tuning (SFT/RLHF) after pretraining is another training run, constructing a new loss from human feedback that reshapes a next-line predictor into a helpful, plain-speaking assistant — day 8's topic.

h.zh: 延伸：这条曲线贯穿后面 163 天

p.zh: 梯度下降是后面所有主题的发动机：第 8 天的「对齐与 RLHF」是把损失函数换成人类偏好，坡的方向随之改变；阶段二的提示工程之所以有效，是因为它不动参数、只挪输入——便宜的「推理时引导」；阶段三 Agent 的微调（fine-tuning）就是在自己的数据上继续走这条下坡；阶段四 RAG 完全绕开训练，用检索补知识，恰恰因为再走一次预训练的下坡贵到不合理。今天带走一句话——
p.en: Gradient descent powers everything ahead: alignment and RLHF (day 8) swap in a human-preference loss, changing where downhill points; prompting (stage 2) works because it steers the input without touching parameters — cheap inference-time guidance; fine-tuning (stage 3) walks the same downhill on your own data; RAG (stage 4) skips training entirely, retrieving knowledge instead — precisely because another pretraining descent is absurdly expensive. One sentence for today —

h.zh: 动手（15 分钟）

p.zh: 不需要 GPU，一支笔一张纸：目标函数 f(w)=(w−3)²，从 w=0 出发手动迭代 w ← w − 学习率 × 2×(w−3)，分别用学习率 0.8 和 2.0 各迭代 5 步，把每步的 w 和 f(w) 记成表格。然后回答：为什么 0.8 的表格收敛到 3 附近，而 2.0 的表格越走越远？（提示：f 在 w 处的坡度是 2×(w−3)，当每步跳过的距离超过谷宽的两倍时，会跳到坡的另一边且落点更高。）
p.en: No GPU needed — pen and paper: for f(w)=(w−3)², iterate w ← w − lr × 2×(w−3) from w=0, five steps each at lr=0.8 and lr=2.0, tabulating w and f(w). Then answer: why does the 0.8 table converge toward 3 while the 2.0 table runs away? (Hint: the slope is 2×(w−3); when each step leaps more than twice the valley width, you land on the other slope, higher than before.)

takeaway.zh: 训练 = 沿损失曲线下坡：模型没有变聪明，只是几千亿个旋钮被误差信号同步拧向「预测更准」的方向——所有智能都是这个目标的副产品。
takeaway.en: Training is a walk downhill on the loss curve: the model never got smarter — billions of knobs were nudged, in sync, toward better next-token prediction. All intelligence is a byproduct of that one goal.

hook.zh: 模型不是背会的，是改错改会的。

sentence.zh: 预测、量误差、朝坡下走一小步。

note.zh: 示意：损失随训练步数下降——前几百步陡降，之后越来越平：容易的规律先学会，剩下的误差越来越难榨。
note.en: Illustrative: loss falls with training steps — steep early, then flattening as the easy patterns are learned first.

coverHook.zh: 训练一次 ≈ 5.9×10²⁰ 次运算：单张 4090 要跑 20 年。
coverHook.en: One training run ≈ 5.9×10²⁰ operations: 20+ years on a single RTX 4090.

title.zh: 注意力：模型怎么决定「看哪里」
title.en: Attention: how the model decides where to look

subtitle.zh: 预测下一个词靠的不是记住全文，而是每一步都在「回头看」：每个 token 给所有 token 打分、按分配额取用信息。这一步是 Transformer 的心脏，也是窗口越长越贵的根源。
subtitle.en: Predicting the next word isn't about memorizing the text — it's about looking back: every token scores every token and borrows information by quota. This is the heart of the Transformer, and the reason longer windows cost more.

h.zh: 机制：每个 token 都在问「谁和我有关」
h.en: Mechanism: every token asks "who here relates to me?"

p.zh: 处理「小猫追球，因为它累了」时，模型怎么知道「它」指小猫？靠注意力。每个 token 发出三个向量：查询（Query，我在找什么）、键（Key，我这里有什么）、值（Value，我的实际内容）。拿「它」的查询和句中每个词的键做点积——方向越一致分越高——除以 √d 缩放后跑一遍第 3 天讲过的 softmax，得到一组总和为 100% 的权重；再把所有词的值向量按权重加权求和，「它」的新表示里就掺进了约九成「小猫」的信息。
p.en: In "The cat chased the ball because it was tired", how does the model know "it" means the cat? Attention. Every token emits three vectors: a Query (what I'm looking for), a Key (what I offer), and a Value (my actual content). Dot the query of "it" with every token's key — aligned directions score higher — scale by √d, run the softmax from day 3, and you get weights summing to 100%; the weighted sum of all value vectors then folds about 90% of "cat" into the new representation of "it".

deep.zh: 为什么是「点积 + softmax」这套组合？点积直接复用第 2 天的几何：query 和 key 是同一种「语义坐标」，夹角小即相关，不必另造相似度算法；softmax（第 3 天）把任意分数压成总和固定的分配比例，保证「取用的信息总量守恒」；除以 √d 是工程补丁——维度越高点积方差越大，不缩放的话 softmax 会饱和成 one-hot，梯度消失、训练不动。而整套设计最大的动机是并行：RNN 要逐词递归，注意力一步看全句——Transformer 能吃下海量数据，全靠这一点。
deep.en: Why dot product plus softmax? The dot product reuses day 2's geometry: query and key live in the same semantic space, small angle means relevant — no separate similarity algorithm needed. Softmax (day 3) squashes arbitrary scores into shares with a fixed total, keeping the borrowed-information budget constant; dividing by √d is an engineering patch — higher dimensions inflate dot-product variance, and unscaled softmax saturates into one-hot, killing gradients. And the biggest design motive is parallelism: RNNs recurse word by word, attention sees the whole sentence in one step — that is exactly what lets Transformers swallow massive data.

h.zh: 算一笔账：窗口越长，评分表平方级爆炸
h.en: The math: longer windows, quadratically exploding score tables

p.zh: 注意力要对「每个位置 × 每个位置」打分——n 个 token 就是 n² 对。128K 窗口约 131,072 个 token：单层单头要算 131,072² ≈ 171.8 亿对；乘上 32 个头、80 层，一次调用约 44 万亿对评分。同一个模型把窗口从 4K 开到 128K，token 数 32 倍，评分量 1,024 倍——平方级。这就是第 4 天「窗口越大越慢越贵」的机制根源：贵的不是读，是每一层都要重打一遍全对全的评分表。
p.en: Attention scores every position against every position — n tokens mean n² pairs. A 128K window is ≈131,072 tokens: 131,072² ≈ 17.2 billion pairs per head per layer; times 32 heads and 80 layers, about 44 trillion pairs per call. Stretching the same model from 4K to 128K grows tokens 32x but score pairs 1,024x — quadratic. That is the mechanism behind day 4's "bigger windows are slower and pricier": the cost isn't reading, it's re-scoring the full all-pairs table at every layer.

h.zh: 实例

p.zh: 一个真实规模的头（示意数值，softmax 实算）：查询「它」，对句中 7 个词打分——「小猫」0.55 → 89.5%、「球」0.25 → 8.1%、「累了」0.0 → 1.1%、「，」−1.2 → 0.0%。softmax 之后每个词分到的权重就是它向「它」输送信息的配额：九成给小猫，其余词几乎分不到。这一个头管「指代」，另一批头各管语法、位置、搭配——多头就是把几十种「关注模式」并联起来。
p.en: One real-scale head (illustrative values, actual softmax): query "it", scoring all 7 tokens — "cat" 0.55 → 89.5%, "ball" 0.25 → 8.1%, "tired" 0.0 → 1.1%, "," −1.2 → 0.0%. After softmax, each weight is that token's quota of information flowing into "it": ~90% to the cat, the rest nearly nothing. This head handles reference; other heads handle syntax, position, collocations — multi-head is dozens of attention patterns wired in parallel.

h.zh: 误区：注意力权重 ≠ 模型的「解释」
h.en: Misconception: attention weights ≠ the model's explanation

p.zh: 把注意力热力图当「模型推理过程的透视」很诱人，但站不住：一是层数——几十层叠起来，第 5 层的权重图解释不了第 40 层的决策；二是多头——几十个头各看各的模式，单独拎出一个头的连线只是盲人摸象；三是权重只是「信息流动的记录」，不是「决策的理由」。同理，「模型像人一样通读并重读全文」也不成立：每个 token 一视同仁、一步并行打分，没有先后和回看——中段信息被稀释（第 4 天的位置偏差），根源正在这里。
p.en: Reading attention heatmaps as an x-ray of the model's reasoning is tempting but doesn't hold: layers — dozens stack up, a layer-5 heatmap can't explain a layer-40 decision; heads — dozens of heads each track their own pattern, one head's lines are a partial glimpse at best; and weights record where information flows, not why a decision was made. Likewise "the model reads like a person, back and forth" is wrong: every token is scored in parallel, no order, no rereading — which is exactly why mid-window content gets diluted (day 4's positional bias).

h.zh: 常见误区

p.zh: 「注意力 = 人类的注意力」。只借了名字：人的注意是主动筛选视野，模型的注意力是一次全对全的加权平均运算——它从不「忽略」任何词，只是给每个词分配 0～1 的输送配额，多数词的配额接近 0。所以说「模型只关注了重点」是误导：它把所有词都算了一遍，只是算完几乎没用上大部分。
p.en: "Attention = human attention." Only the name is borrowed: human attention actively filters the field of view, while model attention is one all-pairs weighted averaging — it never ignores a word, it just assigns each a 0–1 quota, and most quotas are near zero. Saying "the model focused on the key part" misleads: it computed everything, and most of it barely mattered.

h.zh: 延伸：注意力是后面 162 天的舞台

p.zh: 注意力是后面所有主题的共同舞台：阶段二的「上下文工程」本质是给注意力喂料——把最该被打高分的 token 摆进窗口，结构化、去噪声、放首尾；阶段三 Agent 的工具输出要精简，因为几十 KB 的 JSON 会稀释关键信息的权重；阶段四 RAG 是在窗口外先做一次预筛选，只让最相关的段落进赛场；第 8 天的对齐训练改的也是同一台机器——用人类偏好调整注意力与输出模式。今天带走一句话——
p.en: Attention is the shared stage for everything ahead: stage 2's context engineering is feeding it — putting the tokens that should score high into the window, structured, denoised, near the edges; stage 3 agents keep tool outputs lean, because tens of KB of JSON dilute the weights of what matters; stage 4 RAG pre-screens outside the window, letting only the most relevant passages into the arena; and day 8's alignment tunes this same machine with human preferences. One sentence for today —

h.zh: 动手（15 分钟）

p.zh: 不用写代码，一张纸：给「小猫追球，因为它累了」里的查询词「它」手工建一张评分表——给其余 6 个词各打一个 −2～2 的分（越高越相关），自己算或用计算器跑一遍 softmax（取 e 的幂、求和、逐个相除），把权重写成总和 100%。然后回答：为什么「它→小猫」的分差只要拉开一点，权重就会一边倒？（提示：softmax 是指数放大器——分差 0.6 时概率比已是 e^0.6 ≈ 1.8 倍，分差 2 时是 e² ≈ 7.4 倍。）
p.en: No code needed — one sheet of paper: for the query "it" in "The cat chased the ball because it was tired", hand-build a score table — rate the other 6 words from −2 to 2 (higher = more relevant), run softmax yourself (exponentiate, sum, divide), and write the weights as a total of 100%. Then answer: why does even a small score gap tip the weights overwhelmingly toward one word? (Hint: softmax is an exponential amplifier — a 0.6 gap already means a e^0.6 ≈ 1.8x probability ratio; a gap of 2 means e² ≈ 7.4x.)

takeaway.zh: 注意力 = 每个位置向全部位置打分、按分配额取信息：「理解」不是通读并记住，而是每一步动态决定「从谁那里借多少」——代价是一张平方级膨胀的评分表。
takeaway.en: Attention = every position scoring all positions and borrowing information by quota: "understanding" isn't reading and memorizing — it's dynamically deciding whom to borrow from at every step, at the price of a quadratically growing score table.

hook.zh: 「它」指的是谁？模型每处理一个词都要回答一次这个问题。
hook.en: Who is "it"? The model answers this for every single word.

sentence.en: The cat chased the ball because it was tired

note.zh: 查询 =「它」：对句中每个词打分后经 softmax 归一化，权重总和恒为 100%（示意数值，真实 softmax 计算）。权重最高的词是信息的主要来源。
note.en: Query = "it": every token is scored, then softmax normalizes — weights always sum to 100% (illustrative values, real softmax). The top-weighted word is the main information source.

coverHook.zh: 「它」指谁？128K 窗口单层要打 171 亿对分，整次调用 44 万亿对。
coverHook.en: Who is "it"? A 128K window scores 17.1B pairs in one layer — 44 trillion per call.

title.zh: 预训练：从万亿 token 到一个模型
title.en: Pretraining: from trillions of tokens to one model

subtitle.zh: 互联网进去，一个模型出来：清洗、切 token、走几万步梯度下降——预训练不是存储，是有损压缩，把万亿 token 压成一台「只会续写」的预测机器。它是所有大模型应用的毛坯，也是贵到只有少数人付得起的一步。
subtitle.en: The internet goes in, one model comes out: clean, tokenize, descend for tens of thousands of steps — pretraining is lossy compression, squeezing trillions of tokens into a machine that only knows how to continue. It is the blank slate behind every LLM app, and the one step few can afford.

h.zh: 机制：流水线四步，每一步都在筛选
h.en: Mechanism: a four-step pipeline that filters at every stage

p.zh: 预训练是一条流水线。① 收集：从网页、书籍、代码里抓来数万亿 token 的原始语料——先有原料，第 1 天的 BPE 词表这时还没上场；② 清洗去重：给每篇文档算指纹，重复段落只留一份——重复文本会让模型死记硬背而不是学规律，低质内容会直接污染参数；③ 切 token：用 BPE 词表把全部文本变成统一的数字序列（第 1 天）；④ 训练：按第 5 天的梯度下降循环，对每个位置预测下一个 token（第 6 天的注意力负责「看哪里」），误差回传、参数更新，重复几万到几十万步。
p.en: Pretraining is a pipeline. 1) Collect: scrape trillions of tokens of raw corpus from web pages, books, and code — raw material first; the BPE vocabulary of day 1 hasn't entered yet. 2) Clean and dedupe: fingerprint each document, keep one copy of duplicates — repeated text teaches memorization instead of patterns, and low-quality content poisons parameters directly. 3) Tokenize: convert all text into uniform number sequences with the BPE vocabulary (day 1). 4) Train: run the gradient-descent loop from day 5 — predict the next token at every position (day 6's attention decides where to look), backpropagate, update, repeat for tens of thousands of steps.

deep.zh: 为什么整个大厦只押「预测下一个 token」这一个目标？因为它是唯一不需要人工标注的自监督信号——互联网上每段文字自带标准答案（下一个词是什么），数据量上不封顶；而「完形填空」式的目标只见过局部上下文，学不到长程生成。选目标本质是压缩经济学：下一词预测拿到的数据最多，恰好也是生成任务本身的形状——这就是 GPT 路线胜出的设计动机，其余一切能力都是这个单一目标的副产品。
deep.en: Why bet the entire edifice on one objective, next-token prediction? Because it is the only self-supervised signal that needs no human labels — every passage on the internet carries its own ground truth (the next word), so the data supply is unbounded; cloze-style objectives see only local context and never learn long-range generation. Choosing the objective is compression economics: next-token prediction gets the most data and happens to mirror the generation task itself — the design motive behind GPT's win. Everything else is a byproduct of this single target.

h.zh: 算一笔账：15 万亿 token 是什么概念
h.en: The math: what 15 trillion tokens actually means

p.zh: 把 15T token 换算成能感知的量：一本 300 页的书约 20 万字 ≈ 13 万 token，15T token 相当于约 1,150 万本这样的书。算力按第 5 天的公式（6×N×D）估：405B 参数 × 15T token × 6 ≈ 3.6×10²⁵ 次运算。一张 H100 每秒约 4×10¹⁴ 次有效运算，单卡要跑 2,800 多年；Meta 用约 1.6 万张 H100 并行，才把这次运算压进两个月。预训练贵就贵在这里：一次性把人类公开文本整体走一遍梯度下降。
p.en: Convert 15T tokens into something you can feel: a 300-page book is ~200k characters ≈ 130k tokens, so 15T tokens ≈ 11.5 million such books. Compute by day 5's formula (6×N×D): 405B params × 15T tokens × 6 ≈ 3.6×10²⁵ operations. One H100 delivers ~4×10¹⁴ effective FLOP/s — a single card would need 2,800+ years; Meta ran ~16,000 H100s in parallel to squeeze it into two months. That is what pretraining costs: one full pass of gradient descent over humanity's public text.

h.zh: 实例

p.zh: 人类对照：一个人以每秒 5 个 token 的速度不间断阅读 80 年——5 × 3,150 万秒/年 × 80 ≈ 126 亿 token——连 LLaMA 3 训练量（15T）的千分之一都不到。模型在两个月里「读完」了一个人一千多辈子读不完的文本；而前提是这些文本先被清洗到可用——这正是流水线前半段存在的理由。
p.en: The human comparison: reading nonstop at 5 tokens/second for 80 years — 5 × 31.5M s/yr × 80 ≈ 12.6 billion tokens — is not even a thousandth of LLaMA 3's training set (15T). In two months the model reads what one person could not finish in a thousand lifetimes; and that presumes the text was cleaned into usable form first — the very reason the pipeline's front half exists.

h.zh: 误区：预训练不是「把互联网存进硬盘」
h.en: Misconception: pretraining is not "saving the internet to disk"

p.zh: 把预训练想象成下载互联网，是方向性错误。模型 405B 参数按每个 2 字节存约 800GB，而 15T token 的原文有 30TB 起——参数文件不到原文的 3%。它不是存储，是有损压缩：参数里留下的是规律——语法、事实的统计倾向、推理模式——而不是原文本身。代价：压缩必然丢细节，冷门事实被平均掉，所以模型对热门知识对答如流、对冷门事实张冠李戴（幻觉的结构性来源之一）；收益：压出来的规律能泛化到没见过的组合——这是「智能感」的来源。存储与压缩的差别，就是背诵与理解的差别。
p.en: Imagining pretraining as downloading the internet misses the point. A 405B-parameter model stores ~2 bytes per parameter ≈ 800GB, while 15T tokens of raw text run 30TB+ — the parameter file is under 3% of the original. It is not storage but lossy compression: what the parameters keep are patterns — grammar, statistical leanings of facts, reasoning modes — not the text itself. The cost: compression drops detail and averages away obscure facts, which is why models ace popular knowledge and fumble the obscure (one structural source of hallucination). The payoff: the compressed patterns generalize to unseen combinations — the source of the "intelligence" feel. The difference between storage and compression is the difference between memorizing and understanding.

h.zh: 常见误区

p.zh: 「语料越多，模型一定越好」。堆数据解决不了质量与配比：重复的低质文本教会模型复读而不是推理；语言与领域的配比决定模型擅长什么——中英配比失衡的模型中文必然吃亏。LLaMA 3 的做法不是「有多少用多少」，而是清洗分级后，在训练后期对高质量数据加重采样。真实项目里，数据工程（清洗、去重、配比）占用的时间与算力不比训练本身少。
p.en: "More corpus always means a better model." Piling up data cannot fix quality or mix: duplicated low-grade text teaches parroting, not reasoning, and the language/domain mix decides what the model is good at — a skewed Chinese-English ratio caps Chinese performance for sure. LLaMA 3's approach isn't "use everything we have" but grade after cleaning, then upsample high-quality data late in training. In real projects, data engineering (cleaning, dedup, mixing) eats as much time and compute as the training itself.

h.zh: 延伸：预训练只造了毛坯
h.en: Where this leads: pretraining only builds the blank slate

p.zh: 流水线的产物叫「基座模型」，它只会续写、不认识指令——你问「法国的首都是哪」，它可能接着写「德国的首都是哪」：在语料里这确实是下一句最可能的形状。把它变成助手还差一步：第 8 天的对齐训练（SFT/RLHF）用人类示例和反馈再走一轮梯度下降，教它听指令、说人话。再往后：阶段二的提示工程教你不动模型就能引导基座；阶段三的微调是在自己的数据上重跑这条流水线；阶段四 RAG 给这台压缩机器外接一个可随时更新的知识库，补上有损压缩丢掉的事实。今天带走一句话——
p.en: The pipeline's output is a base model: it continues text and doesn't follow instructions — ask "What is the capital of France?" and it may continue "What is the capital of Germany?", because in the corpus that is literally the likeliest next sentence. One step is missing before it becomes an assistant: day 8's alignment (SFT/RLHF) runs another round of gradient descent on human demonstrations and feedback, teaching it to follow instructions and speak plainly. Then: stage 2's prompting steers the base model without touching it; stage 3's fine-tuning reruns this pipeline on your own data; stage 4's RAG bolts a live-updatable knowledge base onto the compression machine, restoring the facts it dropped. One sentence for today —

h.zh: 动手（15 分钟）

p.zh: 不用写代码，用一张纸做「压缩实验」：写一段 60 字左右的话，把它压缩到 15 字以内，再在摘要基础上连压两轮。然后回答两个问题：① 哪类信息最先被你丢掉？（提示：对比专有名词和连接词的存活率——模型的参数也做了同样的取舍，这就是冷门事实更容易出错的机制。）② 压到第三轮，原文还能被还原吗？——不能。这就是有损压缩和「存进硬盘」的本质区别。
p.en: No code — run a "compression experiment" on paper: write ~60 characters of text, compress it to under 15, then compress the summary twice more. Answer two questions: 1) Which kind of information do you drop first? (Hint: compare the survival rate of proper nouns versus connectives — the model's parameters make the same trade, which is exactly why obscure facts fail first.) 2) After three rounds, can the original be restored? No — that is the difference between lossy compression and saving to disk.

takeaway.zh: 预训练是一次有损压缩：自监督的「下一词预测」把万亿 token 的规律压进参数——原文留不下，规律留得下；数据规模决定能力上限，清洗质量决定下限，而刚出厂的这台压缩机器，只会续写。
takeaway.en: Pretraining is lossy compression: self-supervised next-token prediction squeezes the patterns of trillions of tokens into parameters — the text won't fit, the patterns do; data scale sets the ceiling, cleaning quality the floor, and the machine ships knowing only how to continue.

hook.zh: 互联网进去，一个模型出来——中间发生了什么？
hook.en: The internet goes in, one model comes out — what happens in between?

sentence.zh: 清洗 → 切 token → 梯度下降，几万步后收敛。
sentence.en: Clean, tokenize, descend — converging after tens of thousands of steps.

note.zh: 示意：原始语料经清洗去重、BPE 切分后进入梯度下降（第 5 天）——几万步后收敛成一个基座模型。每一步都在筛选与压缩：数据越纯，有效信息密度越高。
note.en: Illustrative: raw corpus is cleaned, deduped, and tokenized via BPE, then enters gradient descent (day 5) — converging into one base model after tens of thousands of steps. Every stage filters and compresses: purer data, denser signal.

coverHook.zh: 15T token 进，800GB 出：预训练丢掉原文、留下规律——1.6 万张 H100 跑两个月才压得完。
coverHook.en: 15T tokens in, 800GB out: pretraining keeps the patterns and discards the text — 16,000 H100s, two months of compression.

title.zh: 对齐：从会续写到会配合
title.en: Alignment: from continuing text to being helpful

subtitle.zh: 预训练造出的是一台续写机器。对齐分两段把它掰成助手：SFT 照着范文模仿，RLHF 从几十万次人类挑选里学出「分寸」——能力没变，行为变了，而奖励只是代理指标，不是「好」本身。
subtitle.en: Pretraining ships a text-completion machine. Alignment reshapes it in two passes: SFT imitates human demonstrations, RLHF distills "judgment" from hundreds of thousands of human picks — ability unchanged, behavior changed, and reward is a proxy, not goodness itself.

h.zh: 机制：SFT 与 RLHF——人类的挑选如何变成损失
h.en: Mechanism: SFT and RLHF — how human picks become a loss

p.zh: 基座模型出厂只会续写（第 7 天）。对齐分两段把它掰成助手。第一段 SFT（监督微调）：人写几万条高质量问答示范，继续用第 5 天的梯度下降让参数模仿这个分布——本质是「照着范文改作文」。第二段 RLHF（人类反馈强化学习）：让模型对同一问题生成多个回答，人类标注员只做一件事——挑出更好的那个；用几十万次这样的两两比较训练出一个「奖励模型」（能给任何回答打分），再用强化学习（常用 PPO）推动模型朝高分方向更新。梯度下降的老骨架没变，变的只是损失函数：从「预测下一个词」换成「人类偏好」。
p.en: A base model only continues text (day 7). Alignment reshapes it in two passes. First SFT (supervised fine-tuning): humans write tens of thousands of high-quality Q&A demonstrations, and the day-5 gradient descent tunes the parameters to imitate that distribution — learning by example. Second RLHF (reinforcement learning from human feedback): the model generates several answers to the same question and human raters do exactly one thing — pick the better one; a few hundred thousand such pairwise comparisons train a reward model (a scorer for any answer), and reinforcement learning (usually PPO) pushes the model toward high-scoring outputs. The gradient-descent skeleton is unchanged; only the loss swaps from "predict the next token" to "human preference".

deep.zh: 为什么是「挑更好的那个」，而不是直接写标准答案？因为写示范贵且覆盖不了开放性问题，而「比较」对人类便宜得多——标注员不需要知道正确答案，只需要审美判断。两两偏好恰好能训练出奖励模型，把「人类什么时候满意」变成一个可计算的分数，之后才能自动化地走梯度。这是 RLHF 最聪明的杠杆：把贵而慢的「生成示范」换成便宜而快的「成对比较」，一次比较同时定义了两个答案的好坏。
deep.en: Why pick the better one instead of writing the ideal answer? Writing demonstrations is expensive and can't cover open-ended questions, while comparing is cheap for humans — raters need taste, not the right answer. Pairwise preferences happen to be exactly what trains a reward model, turning "when are humans satisfied" into a computable score that can then drive gradient descent automatically. That is RLHF's cleverest lever: swap the expensive, slow "write demonstrations" for the cheap, fast "compare pairs" — one comparison prices two answers at once.

h.zh: 实例：InstructGPT 的账——7.7 万次挑选改写一个模型
h.en: Worked example: InstructGPT's ledger — 77k picks rewrote a model

p.zh: InstructGPT（ChatGPT 的前身）论文的数字：SFT 用了约 1.3 万条人类示范，奖励模型训练用了约 3.3 万次比较，PPO 阶段又用了约 3.1 万次比较——总共约 7.7 万次人类操作，就把一个 1750 亿参数的续写机器掰成了听话的助手。对照预训练的 15T token，对齐的人类数据量小到近乎可以忽略，但产品成败恰恰由这一步决定：同一个基座，对齐前让人恼火，对齐后成了 ChatGPT。
p.en: Numbers from the InstructGPT paper (ChatGPT's ancestor): SFT used ~13k human demonstrations, reward-model training ~33k comparisons, the PPO stage another ~31k — about 77k human operations in total to turn a 175B-parameter completion machine into an obedient assistant. Against 15T pretraining tokens the human data is nearly negligible, yet this step decides the product: same base model, infuriating before alignment, ChatGPT after.

h.zh: 实例

p.zh: 自己微调一个开源 7B 模型要花多少：SFT——500 条高质量问答示范，每条平均 500 token，共 25 万 token，一张 RTX 4090 用 LoRA 几小时跑完；RLHF——标注一次偏好比较约 30 秒，1 万次比较就是约 83 个标注工时，还没算训练奖励模型和跑 PPO 的算力。所以个人项目几乎都停在 SFT + DPO（直接偏好优化：跳过单独的奖励模型，直接用偏好对更新策略）。分工很清楚：SFT 教会「格式」，RLHF/DPO 教会「分寸」。
p.en: Fine-tuning an open 7B model yourself: SFT — 500 good Q&A demonstrations at ~500 tokens each, 250k tokens total, hours on one RTX 4090 with LoRA; RLHF — one preference comparison takes a rater ~30 seconds, so 10k comparisons is ~83 annotator-hours, before any reward-model training or PPO compute. That is why hobby projects stop at SFT + DPO (direct preference optimization: no separate reward model, update straight from preference pairs). The division of labor is clear: SFT teaches format, RLHF/DPO teaches tact.

h.zh: 误区：好评不等于好——对齐的对价
h.en: Misconception: liked is not the same as good — what alignment costs

p.zh: 对齐改变的不是能力而是行为分布：基座的知识一点没少，只是从「接话」变成「配合」。它也有对价——「对齐税」：过度对齐的模型会变得胆小、啰嗦、拒绝一切有风险的任务。更隐蔽的是「讨好」（sycophancy）：奖励模型来自人类偏好，而人类天然偏爱顺着自己的回答——你说一个错误观点，对齐后的模型更可能附和「你说得对」。奖励是代理指标，不是「好」本身，Goodhart 定律在这里生效：指标被优化到极致时，就不再代表目标。
p.en: Alignment changes the behavior distribution, not capability: the base model keeps every bit of knowledge, it just moves from "continuing" to "cooperating". But there is a price — the alignment tax: over-aligned models turn timid, verbose, and refuse anything with a whiff of risk. More insidious is sycophancy: the reward model comes from human preferences, and humans naturally favor answers that agree with them — state a wrong opinion and an aligned model is likelier to chime in "you're right". Reward is a proxy metric, not goodness itself; Goodhart's law applies in full: when a measure becomes the target, it ceases to be a good measure.

h.zh: 常见误区

p.zh: 「RLHF 之后模型说的就是对的」。恰恰相反：对齐训练教的是「什么样的回答会被人类点赞」，不是「什么是真的」——幻觉不会因此消失，甚至可能更隐蔽（编得更像人类喜欢的样子，这是第 9 天的主题）。同理，「对齐等于审查」也是误读：拒绝有害请求只是对齐的一小块，它的主体是学会听指令、承认不确定、把握语气分寸——这些是产品能力，不是道德说教。
p.en: "After RLHF the model tells the truth." Quite the opposite: alignment teaches "which answers get liked", not "what is true" — hallucination doesn't disappear and can get sneakier (fabrications shaped more like what humans like to hear — day 9's topic). And "alignment equals censorship" misreads it too: refusing harmful requests is a small slice; the bulk is learning to follow instructions, admit uncertainty, and hold the right tone — product capabilities, not moralizing.

h.zh: 延伸：对齐是产品化的第一步，不是最后一步
h.en: Where this leads: alignment is the first step of productization

p.zh: 对齐把毛坯变成了产品，但也只是第一层：第 9 天的「幻觉与不确定性」要讲对齐没能根治的问题——模型仍会一本正经地编造；阶段二的提示工程建立在对齐模型之上：先理解它被训练成「愿意配合」，才知道怎么把需求讲清楚；阶段三 Agent 的系统提示之所以稳定有效，正是对齐教会了模型尊重指令层级；阶段五会回头看一个更根本的问题——当 AI 替你做判断时，「谁定义了奖励」就是谁定义了价值观。今天带走一句话——
p.en: Alignment turns the blank slate into a product, but it's only the first layer: hallucination and uncertainty (day 9) cover what alignment never fixed — the model still fabricates with total confidence; stage 2's prompting builds on aligned models: understanding that it was trained to cooperate is how you learn to state requirements clearly; stage 3's agent system prompts work reliably because alignment taught the model to respect instruction hierarchy; and stage 5 returns to something deeper — when AI judges for you, whoever defines the reward defines the values. One sentence for today —

h.zh: 动手（15 分钟）

p.zh: 找同一个开源模型的 base 版和 chat 版（如 Llama-3-8B 与其 Instruct 版）各一个在线演示，问三个问题：「法国的首都是哪？」「帮我写一封请假邮件」「1+1 等于几？」，对比两者回答。然后回答：为什么 base 版对第三问可能接着写「2+2 等于几？」，而 chat 版会直接回答 2？（提示：base 版的任务是「续写语料里最常见的下一句」——语料里的算式常以连环形式出现；chat 版被 SFT 教过「问一句，答一句」。）
p.en: Find online demos of the same open model's base and chat versions (e.g. Llama-3-8B and its Instruct variant) and ask three questions: "What is the capital of France?" "Write me a leave-request email." "What is 1+1?" Compare the answers. Then answer: why might the base version continue "What is 2+2?" while the chat version just says 2? (Hint: the base model's job is "write the likeliest continuation" — arithmetic strings often appear in runs in the corpus; the chat version was SFT-taught "one question, one answer".)

takeaway.zh: 对齐 = 用人类的挑选重新定义损失：SFT 教格式、RLHF 教分寸——能力没变，行为变了；奖励是代理指标，被优化到极致就不再等于「好」。
takeaway.en: Alignment = redefining the loss with human picks: SFT teaches format, RLHF teaches tact — ability unchanged, behavior changed; reward is a proxy metric, and pushed to its extreme it stops meaning "good".

hook.zh: 问基座「法国的首都」，它可能反问你「德国的呢」。
hook.en: Ask a base model for France's capital and it may ask you about Germany's.

sentence.zh: 人类挑一次，梯度走一步。
sentence.en: One human pick, one gradient step.

prompt.en: Q: What is the capital of France?

a.en: What is the capital of Germany?

b.en: The capital of France is Paris.

a.zh: 巴黎。（参见《世界百科》第 827 页）
a.en: Paris. (See Encyclopedia of the World, p. 827)

b.zh: 是巴黎。需要我简单介绍一下吗？
b.en: It's Paris. Want a quick intro?

note.zh: 示意：每一轮人类挑出更好的回答，奖励模型学会打分，策略胜率随之爬升（对齐后的偏好胜率）。
note.en: Illustrative: each round a human picks the better answer, the reward model learns to score, and the policy's win rate climbs (preference win rate after alignment).

coverHook.zh: 问「法国的首都」，基座模型反问你「德国的呢」——7.7 万次人类挑选把它改好了。
coverHook.en: Ask for France's capital, get asked about Germany's — 77k human picks fixed that.
